title: Multisig modules and guards are forbidden unless explicitly permitted for the use case
content:
A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.1 is a one-line prohibition: "[m]ultisigs must not utilize any modules or guards, except those explicitly permitted for the applicable use case in [Use-Case Specific Configuration Requirements]."

The severity is proportionate to what modules do. In Safe-style wallets, an enabled module can execute transactions *without* satisfying the signing threshold — it is an authorized bypass of the entire security model the rest of this framework builds. A guard can likewise block or alter execution. Both are legitimate tools and both silently invalidate every threshold assumption a reviewer would otherwise make from the signer configuration.

Choosing default-deny rather than default-allow-with-review is the right shape here because the failure is invisible: a multisig with a malicious module looks identical on-chain to a compliant one unless someone specifically enumerates modules. An allowlist means an auditor checking compliance has a closed set to compare against.

The cost is friction — every legitimate automation needs a use-case entry added to the Atlas before it can be used. The framework accepts that cost, and the only allowlisted case in this chunk is the Treasury allowance module of A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.2.1.
description: A default-deny rule on Safe extensions: no modules or guards at all except those allowlisted per use case, because a module can bypass the signing threshold entirely.
